description: A tree of floodplain (varzea), riverbank, secondary/gaps, 36-51 m tall (to 60 m). Bole straight and cylindrical, usually spiny (UTP). width_m is the stated maximum ('up to 60 m'). Fruit: pendant, elliptic, brown, five-valved capsule, about 15 cm (Spanish Wikipedia), with 66-250 seeds of 4-6 mm in pale yellow kapok fibre; wind-dispersed.

notes: Template shorea_leprosula: an emergent: a buttressed clear bole under an umbrella crown (light red meranti). Briefly deciduous by the sources, but no months given: drawn evergreen. NOT SOURCED (the template's or a default value): crown depth (the template's); leaf colour (a tropical evergreen's mid green); bark colour (the template's); bark texture (the template's). Research notes: Height: Wikipedia to 60 m, UTP to 70 m. UTP's typical 10-30 m covers the whole range including secondary growth, so typical height is left null for the wild emergent. Diameter: Spanish Wikipedia about 3 m. Habitat (UTP): emergent in moist evergreen and semi-deciduous forests including seasonally flooded ones, plus gallery and dry forests; mostly in secondary forest as a pioneer; to 1200 m (Spanish Wikipedia 0-1500 m). 'riverbank' reads UTP's gallery forest. Phenology: no Madre de Dios or Osa months found. Spanish Wikipedia (no region given, likely Mesoamerica) says it drops its leaves at the start of the dry season, flowers Dec-Mar (not every year) and fruits Apr-Jun. English Wikipedia says it flowers while briefly leafless. UTP says leafing and flowering are highly irregular in moist areas. In central Amazonia, 17 of 21 trees flowered once or twice in six years (Gribel et al. 1999), so mass flowering is supra-annual there. Leafless months unknown. Flowers open at night with a strong odour. Visitors (Gribel): bats, marsupials, night monkeys, hawkmoths, bees, wasps and hummingbirds; only phyllostomid bats matter for pollination. No source read named animals eating its seeds or leaves (a diet-overlap database listing Ateles paniscus and Ara macao was not used).
